pure-announcement.rationale: This is the protocol's own dedicated security-considerations document, not a launch or release note.

duplicate.rationale: Its mix-up-attack section overlaps mcp-authorization-hardening, but confused deputy, token passthrough, SSRF via OAuth discovery, state handle hijacking, local server compromise, authorization-URL validation, stdio proxy escalation and scope minimization are mechanisms neither mcp-authorization-hardening nor mcp-attack-surface-taxonomy details — a reader of both existing concepts still learns substantial new mechanism here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: It is the official spec's own security document, cross-referencing specific RFCs (9207, 9068, 9728) with reproducible attack flows and MUST/SHOULD-level protocol requirements.

durability.rationale: These are protocol-level attack mechanisms and their structural mitigations, not version numbers or a feature matrix, so they hold up the way a threat model holds up rather than the way a stat holds up.

actionability.rationale: Nearly every attack class ends in explicit MUST/SHOULD engineering requirements a builder can implement directly, not a described landscape.

atomicity.rationale: The note bundles roughly nine largely independent attack mechanisms (confused deputy, token passthrough, SSRF, state handle hijacking, local server compromise, OAuth URL validation, stdio proxy escalation, mix-up attacks, scope minimization) rather than one core idea stateable in a paragraph — it should be split, and only the mechanisms not already covered by mcp-authorization-hardening or mcp-attack-surface-taxonomy are worth extracting.
